title: adaptive-slot-rebalance-to-address-queue-skew-and-starvation
author: Asha Nair
description:
Motivation: Long-tail request patterns + heterogeneous KV cache hits were causing persistent queue skew across worker shards in the continuous batching scheduler. Small tenants and short sequences were starved behind heavy streaming requests that pinned KV caches, causing visible latency regressions for 95th/99th percentiles. This change introduces an adaptive slot rebalance controller that re-evaluates per-shard slot allocations on soft timeouts and when skew thresholds are exceeded.

Summary of changes: - Add a slot rebalance controller that computes a skew score across scheduling queues and issues low-cost token transfers between shards when imbalance is detected. - Integrate a short randomized graceful drain period to avoid coordinated preemption waves; this uses jittered timeouts and a small credit buffer to preserve KV pin locality where beneficial. - Introduce a lightweight probe sample that estimates per-tenant KV cache pressure and factors it into rebalance decisions (heuristic only; does not evict). - Tune default soft-timeout thresholds and make them configurable via scheduler config (continuous_batcher.rebalance.*). - Add observability: new metrics continuous_batcher.rebalance.skew_ratio, rebalance.attempts, rebalance.success_rate, and per-tenant probe_kv_pressure.

Design notes: - The rebalance controller is intentionally conservative: transfers only occur when skew_ratio > 1.8 or when a soft-timeout has fired 3x in a 30s sliding window. Transfers are limited to at most 10% of a shard's active slots per minute to avoid oscillation. - To reduce KV pin churn we prefer transferring slots associated with requests that have low KV residency (stateless/short sequences) first; longer lived KV-pinned sessions are avoided if probe_kv_pressure indicates high locality. - All heuristics are feature-gated behind continuous_batcher.rebalance.enabled and default to off for Dedicated customers unless explicitly enabled.

Backwards compatibility and rollout: - Default to off for existing clusters. - Feature flag gated + canary rollout via console (1% clusters -> 10% -> 50% -> global). - Includes automatic rollback hook if 95th latency increases by >10% or error-rate climbs >1% in canary buckets.

Benchmarks: - Synthetic mixed workload (70% short seq <64 tokens, 25% medium, 5% long streaming) on 8-shard cluster: 95th latency reduced 18%, 99th reduced 12%, tail throughput increased 6%. - KV-heavy skew scenario (two heavy tenants on shards 3/4): starvation events dropped from 23 to 3 per hour in load tests. Full benchmark logs attached in CI artifact.

What changed (high level file map): - scheduler/rebalance/controller.go (new): core rebalance logic and heuristics - scheduler/rebalance/probe.go (new): lightweight KV pressure probe - scheduler/batcher/continuous.go (modified): hook points for drain and token transfer - config/schema.yaml (modified): new rebalance config knobs - observability/metrics_registry.go (modified): metric registration - tests/scheduler/rebalance_test.go (new): unit tests for skew detection - e2e/perf/bench_rebalance.yaml (new): perf harness for canary

Commits (summary): - f3a9c7e: initial controller scaffolding and config knobs - b28d411: add probe, integrate with scheduler hooks - 7a5d2c4: add metrics and dashboard queries - e13b4d9: tests and benchmark harness - 4f11a21: benchmark tuning, flake fixes, docs - 9c0fef2: enable feature flag, canary rollout manifest

Review conversation (highlights): - Reviewer (Liam Carter): "Can we ensure transfers respect tenant isolation boundaries? Also please add a flag to disable KV-probe influence for enterprise customers who want strict locality." - Author reply (Asha Nair): "Added enterprise bypass flag continuous_batcher.rebalance.ignore_kv_probe and unit test to verify bypass path." - Reviewer (Marta Reyes): "Concern about oscillation under bursty traffic." - Author reply: "Added exponential backoff and an overall per-shard transfer cap (10%/min), included in design notes and unit tests." - Approvals: Liam Carter (approved), Marta Reyes (approved after adjustments), SRE rotation (auto-approve CI pass).

CI: initial flaky test in scheduler suite; re-ran unit tests and e2e perf. CI artifacts include perf logs and a flamegraph showing reduced wait-time.

Merge: merged via squash on 2026-03-02 after successful canary smoke and CI green.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests added - [x] Benchmarks and perf harness added - [x] Feature flag and config documented - [x] Observability metrics added - [x] Rollout + rollback documented

Related work and references: Linear tickets: ENG-1427 (scheduler stability), ENG-1669 (kv cache telemetry). Related PRs: none that directly rebalanced slots; complements recent continuous-batcher timeout tuning PRs.
